name: Google Keep
tagline: Sticky-note style notes, checklists and reminders that sync across your Google account.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Keep is free with a Google account and bundled into Google Workspace tiers rather than sold on its own.

verdictSummary: Keep is a text box, a checkbox, a color picker and a search field. There is no clever algorithm, no proprietary corpus, no network of other users making your notes better. An agent can produce a local notes app with pinning, labels, colors, checklists and full text search in a single sitting, and the data model is roughly one table. The honest catch is that Keep is free and already on your phone, so the DIY version competes on ownership rather than on price. Build it if you want your notes in a file you control, not because Google is squeezing you.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you create, color, pin, label, search and archive note cards and checklists, stored in SQLite.
requirements: Somewhere to run it if you want phone access, a home server or a small VPS
whatYouLose: Native Android and iOS apps with an offline cache and home screen widgets
Instant sync across every device you own without you thinking about hosting
Share a note with someone else and watch them edit it live
OCR on photos of receipts and whiteboards, plus voice notes with transcription
Deep Google plumbing: reminders that surface in Calendar and Assistant, notes in the Docs sidebar
moatNotes: The stickiness is distribution, not the software. It ships with the Google account you already have and lives in the sidebar of things you already open.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays for Keep directly, which is the whole point: it arrives free with an account most people cannot leave, it is already installed, and it syncs to a phone without anyone configuring anything. That is a distribution moat rather than a product moat. The people who leave usually do so for privacy or portability, not because they found something dramatically better at holding short text.
notes: The easiest kind of one-shot: a CRUD app wearing a color palette.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted quick-notes app, a personal replacement for Google Keep. Empty folder, no scaffolding beyond what you install.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify for the server
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/notes.db, WAL mode
- Server-rendered HTML with a small amount of vanilla JS, no React, no build step
- FTS5 virtual table for full text search

Data model:
- notes: id, title, body, kind ('text' or 'list'), color, pinned, archived, trashed, created_at, updated_at
- list_items: id, note_id, text, checked, position
- labels: id, name; note_labels join table
- notes_fts mirroring title and body, kept in sync with triggers

Features in scope:
- Masonry grid of note cards, pinned notes in a separate section on top
- Create a text note or a checklist note; checklist items are addable, checkable, reorderable by drag, and checked items sink to the bottom
- Eight background colors, set from a swatch row on each card
- Labels: create, attach, filter by label in a left sidebar
- Archive and trash, with a trash view and a permanent delete
- Search box hitting FTS5, matching title, body and list item text
- Autosave on blur and on a 800ms debounce while typing, no save buttons
- Keyboard: 'c' to create, '/' to focus search, Escape to close the editor
- GET /export returns all notes as JSON; POST /import accepts the same shape

Explicitly out of scope: accounts, multi-user, sharing, OAuth, telemetry, any cloud service, OCR, voice notes, reminders and notifications. Single trusted user on a private network.

Also deliver:
- .env for PORT and DB_PATH, with a .env.example, no secrets in code
- npm run dev and npm run start
- A responsive layout that is actually usable on a phone browser, since that is where notes get written
- A README with setup, a note on backing up the sqlite file, and a one-paragraph section on putting it behind Tailscale or a reverse proxy with basic auth if you want it off-LAN
- Seed script inserting a handful of example notes so the grid is not empty on first run
